plain_text:
The best-known of all sports songs got its
start on the New York subway, where Jack
Norworth jotted down the lyrics in 1908.
Albert Von Tilzer set the words to music,
launching a century of “root, root, root for
the home team” singalongs at ballparks
across America. Norworth and Von Tilzer
submitted this sheet music of the song to
the U.S. Copyright Office at the Library for
copyright on May 2, 1908.

plain_text:
Jackie Robinson broke baseball's color line
in 1947, a historic moment in the history of
the game and the nation. Three years later,
he starred in his own biopic,
“The Jackie
Robinson Story.
” This copy of the script, part
of the papers of sportswriter Arthur Mann,
bears the signature of Robinson and co-star
Ruby Dee and Mann's sketches of Dodgers
general manager Branch Rickey and Clyde
Sukeforth, who played a key role in bringing
Robinson to the team.

Below it, credits read “WORDS BY JACK NORWORTHY” and “MUSIC BY ALBERT VON TILZER,” set against decorative light green swirls. At the bottom, silhouettes of a cheering crowd are visible above publisher details: “THE YORK MUSIC CO., NEW YORK” and price “5¢.” A partial line at the very top reads “THE SENSATIONAL...” suggesting additional text cut off by the crop. The layout is vertically oriented with strong typographic hierarchy and early 20th-century graphic design elements.

The image shows a signed copy of “The Jackie Robinson Story,” featuring two pencil sketches: one of a man in profile wearing glasses and holding a cigar (top right), and another of a man in a hat and glasses (bottom left). The title is printed centrally in bold, block letters. Numerous handwritten signatures in blue ink surround the text and illustrations, including names such as Jackie Robinson, Dave Brubeck, Louie Seaver, Jimmie Dodd, Richard Lacy, Sam Levenson, Meek Robinson, Maurice M. Sussman, Bill Spaulding, Ben Winkler, Jack Burgeon, Ernest Labos, Joseph H. Blakely, Rosa Hunter, Julius Gentry, Harry Shannon, Gene Throcks, Howard McManus, Alice E. Brown, Bobby Watson, and others.
